title: Agent tools: seven private modules plus registration

details.goal: Answer is the graph current and what does it cover, including for paths that were never indexed.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'status', description: the verbatim text from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 2, profile:'agent'} and input {paths: array of string optional, budget: integer default 800}. handler.ts exports handle(ctx, args) returning handle(env) built only via constructors from #shared/envelope and sized only via #shared/budget emit. Reads: meta for project_name, project_root, generation, indexed_at, indexer_state, consecutive_failures; latest generation row; file rows plus not_indexed rows for each requested path using prefix ranges; census by language derived from file.parse_status and not_indexed.language. Payload keys exactly: project{name,root,commit,db_path}, graph{nodes,edges,size_bytes,db_path}, languages[{language,files,parsed,failed,note?}], paths[{path,indexed,symbols?,sha256?,reason?}], health{indexer,last_publish_ms,consecutive_failures}. A requested path with no file row and no not_indexed row must appear with indexed:false and reason not_indexed_unknown. This tool owns no other module and imports only #shared/*.

details.goal: One free-text input returns the resolved symbol and its neighbours grouped by relation, with a working resume path.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'trace', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 3, profile:'agent'} and input {query: string required, direction: enum all|in|out default all, kinds: array optional, depth: integer default 2 min 1 max 4, budget: integer default 3200, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts: first, if args.cursor is present, call ctx.cursor.verify(cursor, {tool:'trace', argsHash, generation}) where argsHash covers every other argument; on cursor_invalid, cursor_expired or cursor_mismatch return envelope fail with that code and the hint re-run the original call — never return a partial page. On ok, resume from the decoded position instead of starting at the first item. Then resolve via #shared/domain/resolve; on ambiguous return envelope ambiguous with up to 5 candidates and no payload body; on not_found return not_found with near_misses; on ok call #shared/domain/neighbors expand and shape the payload. Payload keys exactly: resolution{query,matched,kind,how,confidence}, node{id,qn,kind,file,lines,signature,is_test}, in[] and out[] as arrays of {edge,tier,items[{id,qn,kind,file,line,hop,external?,is_test?}]}, unresolved[{file,line,name,evidence,tier}], not_indexed[]. Groups ordered calls, inherits, implements, references, tested_by, imports — the order is fixed and empty groups are omitted. Pass the payload to emit(env, args.budget, {mint: position => ctx.cursor.sign({generation, tool:'trace', argsHash, position})}) so truncation produces a resumable next. Never include source text.

tasks.title: Tool module: summary (change, repo, area scopes)

details.goal: The hottest path: a few hundred tokens that say what changed, how risky it is and what to call next, resumable by cursor.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'summary', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 4, profile:'agent'} and input {scope: enum change|repo|area default change, target: string optional, base: string optional defaulting to the generation base_commit, budget: integer default 1200, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts FIRST verifies args.cursor when present via ctx.cursor.verify(cursor, {tool:'summary', argsHash, generation}) and returns envelope fail with cursor_invalid, cursor_expired or cursor_mismatch and the hint re-run the original call, never a partial page; on ok it resumes from the decoded position. It then dispatches on scope and must not compute repo or area aggregates on the change path. Payload keys — change: base, changed_files[], changed_symbols[{id,qn,kind,change,lines,risk}], risk{score,band,drivers[]}, test_gaps[{qn,reason}], removed_symbols[], suggested_next[{tool,query?,why}]; repo: size{files,nodes,edges}, languages[], entry_points[{qn,kind,reachable}], coupling_hotspots[{qn,in,out}], flows[{name,steps,files}], not_indexed[]; area: target, surface[{qn,kind}], dependents_total, risk. risk.drivers are sentences, never a bare float. Emit through emit(env, args.budget, {mint: position => ctx.cursor.sign({generation, tool:'summary', argsHash, position})}). Reads come from ctx.reader only: metaFor, latestGeneration, changedSince via the diff module, entryPoints, hotspots, testGaps, removedSymbolsFor.

details.goal: Find a declaration when the caller knows roughly what it is called, with stable and resumable ordering.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'search', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 5, profile:'agent'} and input {query: string required, kind: enum function|method|class|file|decorator optional, path: string optional prefix filter, budget: integer default 2000, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts FIRST verifies args.cursor when present via ctx.cursor.verify(cursor, {tool:'search', argsHash, generation}) and returns envelope fail with the cursor code and hint on mismatch, resuming from the decoded position. It then calls ctx.reader.readNodeFts(query, limit) — the reader exposes the FTS5 MATCH because Drizzle cannot model the virtual table — which already orders by bm25 ascending, then in_degree descending, then id ascending, so pagination is stable; apply the optional kind and path filters after the read and keep the documented order. Payload keys: mode ('bm25' in the MVP), results[{id,qn,kind,file,lines,signature?,degree{in,out},score}]. Emit through emit(env, args.budget, {mint: position => ctx.cursor.sign({generation, tool:'search', argsHash, position})}). Never returns source text.

manifest.ts: manifest {name:'search', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md §5 (three sentences joined with single spaces), profile:'agent'}; input {query string required, kind enum function|method|class|file|decorator, path string, budget integer default 2000, cursor string}; SEARCH_KINDS/SearchKind and DEFAULT_BUDGET_TOKENS exported so the handler imports the same numbers the schema advertises. `test` is not a kind because the index stores it as node.is_test, not as a kind value.

handler.ts: cursor verify-before-work via ctx.cursor.verify(cursor,{generation,tool:'search',argsHash}) where argsHash = sha256 of [trimmedQuery, kind|null, normalizedPrefix] — budget is deliberately excluded so a page can be resumed with a larger budget; refusals return envelope fail with the cursor module's own code+hint (test asserts readNodeFts is called 0 times on a refusal). Then readNodeFts(query, 200) — READER_BOUND is a statement bound, documented as such — and kind/path filters applied after the read with isUnderPrefix (so `src` excludes `src-old`), never re-sorting. position is an index into the flattened filtered list; mint(dropped) signs position start+(window.length-dropped), so page 2 continues with no duplicates. Payload {mode:'bm25', results[{id,qn,kind,file,lines,signature?,degree{in,out},score}]}; signature omitted (never undefined) when the row has none; degree from metricsFor(id), null metrics -> 0/0; no source text. emit(env, args.budget ?? 2000, {mint}); budget_too_large (ceiling or a page where nothing fits) is returned as fail, never thrown; bootstrapping when no generation is published. read_status is graph-side: stale when a file in scope was written by an earlier generation (stale_reason + stale_checked_at), omitted stale_checked_at for a repo-wide scope that compared no file; coverage/relation via assemble over exactly the filtered prefix, so a repo-wide search reports complete:false and gte rather than claiming the whole tree.

Change set comes from args.paths or the diff module; expand inbound from those nodes to depth; attach tested_depth and is_entry from node_metrics through the reader. Payload keys: changed[{path,symbols,entry_point}], impacted[{id,qn,kind,hop,via,tier,tested,entry_point?}], unmatched_files[{path,reason}], risk{score,band,drivers[]}. details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'expand', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 7, profile:'agent'} and input {target: string required, what: enum members|edges|source|coverage optional, budget: integer default 2500}. handler.ts resolves target as an id, qn or path; infers what by kind when absent (file or class to members, function or method to edges, folder to coverage) and echoes the choice in payload.what plus payload.why as a sentence such as inferred: class -> members. tasks.title: Register the seven tools in the composition root with profiles

details.goal: Make the server surface exactly seven tools with profiles, a live watcher, clean shutdown and wired next_tools.
details.contract: src/index.ts imports the seven manifests explicitly (no directory scanning), builds ToolContext {reader, cursor, log, now, config}, registers with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer using registerTool with the manifest description and a JSON Schema produced from the manifest input, and MUST ALSO: (1) select the profile from CODEGRAPH_PROFILE (default agent) where agent registers six tools and admin registers all seven, with the same selector driving the tools/list response; (2) start the watcher by calling startWatch imported relatively from ./indexer/watch.ts — a root-only import, never through #shared and never from a tool — when running mcp mode and CODEGRAPH_NO_WATCH is unset, keeping the handle so the exit path calls stop(); (3) install SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that stop the watcher, release the write lock and close the database; (4) populate next_tools on every response from nextToolsFor(tool) imported from #shared/instructions; (5) wire the open-time guard from DATABASE.md section 5 (root_mismatch as a stale_reason, wrong_project_db, unsupported_filesystem, schema_too_new as refusals); (6) catch every handler throw into envelope fail with an AppError code, mapping budget_too_large and index_locked through unchanged. Must never write to stdout. index and status modes run the CLI equivalents and exit.

details.contract: watch.ts exports startWatch(opts: {repoRoot, dataDir, intervalMs default 2000, debounceMs default 500, onSpawn?}): {stop()}. Poll every intervalMs: read git HEAD via git rev-parse HEAD and the working-tree signature via git status --porcelain, plus mtime of tracked files newer than the last generation; when the signature differs from the last observed one, wait debounceMs, re-check, then Bun.spawn bin/codegraph.ts worker and record the exit code. On exit 75 (lock held) log and retry on the next tick without counting a failure. On exit 1 increment an in-memory failure counter and back off to min(intervalMs << failures, 300000). A repository that is not a git checkout degrades to mtime-only detection. Never writes the database itself and never imports the worker module. On stop(), kill a running child and resolve.
details.goal: Keep the graph current without putting the writer in the server process.
